newsitem.title: UK: Ford confirms UK state aid request.
newsitem.headline: Ford confirms UK state aid request.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, the U.S. car giant which announced 1,300 job cuts at its Halewood plant in Liverpool last week, on Monday confirmed reports it had asked for government aid to maintain production there after the year 2000.
A Ford spokeswoman said the company had raised the issue of aid under the government's regional assistance scheme at a meeting last week with Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang.
"We believe the request is under consideration," a spokeswoman said. She did not put a figure on the request.
The car manufacturer announced last week tha 1,300 jobs would have to go at Halewood as the group planned to make the new Escort car model in continental Europe.

The decision has placed the future of the Halewood plant in doubt, although Ford has indicated it would consider building an unspecified new vehicle there after 2000 subject to improved productivity and job flexibility.

Ford workers are holding a series of mass meetings around the country this week over the job cuts at Halewood. Union leaders meet management on Thursday and are expected to make a decision afterwards on whether or not to hold a strike ballot.
